paragraphs: Bar Pada. He and R' Yohanan disagree, Hullin 124b. Tosafot, Temurah 10a, write: ‘This bar Pada is bar Kappara's sister's son, as found in Me'ilah 4b: bar Kappara said to bar Pada, his sister's son, “Consider what you will ask me tomorrow.” This is not ben Pedat, for ben Pedat is R' Elazar.’ End quotation. Our reading in Me'ilah is ‘to bar Pedat, his sister's son,’ etc.; in the new Talmud editions they did not correct it. See R' Elazar bar R' Pedat concerning Yuhasin's error. See what I wrote under R' Hiyya bar Adda, bar Kappara's sister's son. In the Arukh, entry זחל, citing Pesikta of Parah: ‘Bar Pada's face zahalin,’ meaning his face brightened. Rav Bibi in bar Pada's name. R' Pinhas and R' Yirmeyah in the name of R' Hiyya bar Abba: Midrash Kohelet on ‘Woe to you, O land.’ Ilfa; א״ל [‘said to him’; speaker/attachment unresolved]; R' Yaakov in bar Pada's name (see above, Akiva the amora). ‘R' Mattana said,’ etc.; ‘bar Pada said,’ Nazir 5a. Ulla said in bar Pada's name: ‘R' Meir used to say’; when Ravin came, he explained in bar Pada's name, Kiddushin 54b. See above, R' Yehudah ben Pedaya, bar Kappara's sister's son.
